title: Club Brugge at San Siro today, and what Chivu said
description: Cristian Chivu says the dream of a European run has to become a responsibility, and Inter’s 2025/26 accounts show €518 million in revenue and a €22.7 million profit.
mast_alt: Nerazzurri Daily Edition No. 42, Tuesday, October 13, 2026 — Club Brugge at San Siro today, and what Chivu said

blocks.html: Inter host Club Brugge at San Siro today at 3:00 PM ET. It is the second match of the Champions League league phase, and Inter’s first at home. Cristian Chivu, Inter’s head coach, said on Monday that the dream of a European run “has to become a responsibility,” and that Hakan Çalhanoğlu, the midfielder, is fit. The two clubs have never met in a competitive match.

blocks.h3: Chivu: the dream has to become a responsibility
paras: Chivu took the pre-match press conference at Appiano Gentile, Inter’s training ground, on Monday. He said the club’s standing demands that it chase every objective. There are no easy matches in the Champions League, he said, and he does not want his team to lose its identity even in defeat.

On the squad, Chivu said Çalhanoğlu is fit, and that “we’ll make a few changes.” Alessandro Bastoni, the defender, is available. Djed Spence, the wing back, is training again and played 25 minutes against Parma. Chivu said he is “getting fitter.” He also thanked Yann Sommer, Inter’s goalkeeper for three years, who is in Club Brugge’s goal today.

blocks.h3: Akanji wants the top eight, and a home win first
paras: Manuel Akanji, the Inter defender, spoke after his coach. He said the aim is to “finish in the top eight” of the league phase, and that it starts with a win at San Siro. He refused to call the match must-win: six league-phase matches follow this one.

blocks.h3: The accounts: €518 million in revenue and a second straight profit
paras: Inter’s shareholders approved the 2025/26 financial statements on Monday. Revenue was €518 million, the club’s second-highest figure. Only 2024/25 was higher, at €567 million, lifted by the FIFA Club World Cup and the 2025 Champions League final. Net profit was €22.7 million, a second profitable year in a row. Giuseppe Marotta, Inter’s president and chief executive, spoke at the meeting, and the club published its first sustainability report.

blocks.h3: Gazzetta dello Sport expects six changes, and a first start for Stanković
paras: Gazzetta dello Sport, Italy’s biggest sports daily, reported on Monday night that Chivu will make six changes from the side that beat Parma. The least predictable, the paper says, is a first Inter start for Aleksandar Stanković. Inter signed the midfielder in July, after a season at Club Brugge. Gazzetta puts Nicolò Barella and Piotr Zieliński either side of him, with Akanji and Bastoni back in defense.
blocks.kicker: GAZZETTA DELLO SPORT VIA FCINTERNEWS · OCT 12

blocks.h3: Sky Sport Italia’s lineup differs in one place
paras: Sky Sport Italia published its own projected lineup on Monday morning, and it agrees almost everywhere. It has Josep Martínez in goal behind Yann Bisseck, Akanji and Bastoni. Andy Diouf and Federico Dimarco play wide, with Lautaro Martínez and Marcus Thuram together in attack. The one difference is the deep midfield place, which Sky gives to Çalhanoğlu rather than Stanković.
